text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"CA","level":"state","category":"algorithmic_rent_setting","status":"in_force","title":"Cartwright Act: ban on use or distribution of common pricing algorithms (AB 325)","requirement":"It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce. It is also unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt the price or commercial term it recommends for the same or similar products or services in California. A 'common pricing algorithm' is any methodology, including a computer, software or other technology, used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or otherwise influence a price or commercial term. The bill also lets Cartwright Act complaints plead only facts making a contract, combination or conspiracy plausible, without having to exclude the possibility of independent action (B&P Code § 16756.1).
